applies_why: The judge text resolves a collision between the challenger's footed chain and Matthew 1:20 by citing the pressed sentence's own words, which is the verse-by-verse move K-C governs.
quote: the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: "never verse by verse": one reading is that the judge may still cite the pressed verse's own words when finding a link underdetermined; the other is that a footed opposing chain must be weighed against the whole defending chain, not answered by the pressed sentence's wording alone.
why: The judge uses Matthew 1:20's own wording as the counter to the challenger's footed chain, which is verse-by-verse instead of chain-against-chain by footing.
